newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates, bonds idle, ecu/drachma ranges.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates, bonds idle, ecu/drachma ranges.

text.p: Greek interbank depos and forex forwards were little changed, holding late Friday levels, bonds were fluctuating in tight ranges and ecu/drachma was easier, dealers said.
"The market is very quiet, liquidity conditions are better and interbank depos and forex forwards are idling," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Other traders said the overnight rate could ease further on deposits made by utilities and other state entities.

"The central bank is also going to pay interest to commercial banks on their reserves and this is going to boost liquidity pushing the overnight rate lower later on," said a senior private bank dealer.
Reserve requirements currently stand at 12 percent but the central bank pays an interest rate of 11 percent to half of the reserves and nil on the balance.
Bonds were consolidating in the absence of trading incentives with most players focusing on Tuesday's auction of 12-month T-bill and two-year zeros, dealers said.
"There is no major price movement so far," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "It is very calm and the market seems to focus on tomorrow's issue of T-bills and two-year zeros."
Greece will issue 12-month T-bills and two-year zeros at a gross rate of 9.60 percent and 9.50 percent respectively.
"Sales might cover expiries but that's about it. Rates are not that attractive to lure investors," said a bond dealer.
The mark was quoted at 157.73/83 from Friday's 157.905 fix, the dollar at 274.10/20 drachmas from 273.000 and the ecu at 309.64/74 from 309.700 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.70 but has eased a bit to 309.60/65," saida senior private bank dealer.
